review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its only @[simp] (specOverIsoOfAlgEquiv_hom), the isomorphism-hom and compatibility lemmas, and their downstream uses (ComponentFibers.lean and the SchemePropertiesExamples files). I also compared the reassoc/simp conventions in other SchemeProperties files and the duplicate helper in ComponentProduct.lean. I found no rewrite cycles or competing rules. Both findings are about missing or inconsistent simp attributes. I did not run Lean, so I have not tested whether the proposed attributes are confluent or how they interact with the existing simp set. For example, I did not check how a simp-tagged comparison lemma would interact with the pullback simp lemmas that the proof of toComponentScheme_comp_componentBaseChangeComparison already calls via `simp`.

findings.problem: componentBaseChangeIso is a non-reducible def. The only normal form that lets the isomorphism be related to the rest of the API is its forward map, componentBaseChangeComparison. Nothing tags the lemma componentBaseChangeIso_hom for simp, so every user has to rewrite by hand. ComponentFibers.lean does exactly that with `rw [componentBaseChangeIso_hom]` before applying the compatibility lemma. The orientation is already canonical: iso.hom is rewritten to the single comparison constant, so there is no cycle risk and no competing rule.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `componentBaseChangeIso_hom` with `@[simp]`, so `(componentBaseChangeIso X).hom` normalises to `componentBaseChangeComparison X`. Do the same for the private model-level lemma `componentBaseChangeComparisonModelIso_hom`, which normalises to `componentBaseChangeComparisonModel`. Optionally add `@[reassoc]`, which the library already pairs with simp for such morphism identities, to get `e.hom ≫ g` forms.
findings.benefit: Goals that mention the iso and the comparison map can be closed by `simp`. Callers no longer need the manual `rw [componentBaseChangeIso_hom]` step.

findings.excerpt:
toComponentScheme (schemeBaseChange X (L := K)) ≫
        componentBaseChangeComparison (K := K) X =
      baseChangeMap (L := K) (toComponentScheme X)
findings.problem: This is the canonical triangle identity. Its left side is a composite of two canonical maps, and its right side is a single map. It carries neither `@[reassoc]` nor `@[simp]`, although other files in this library use `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]` for the same kind of morphism-composition identity. Because `comparison` is a def, simp cannot reduce `toComponentScheme _ ≫ componentBaseChangeComparison _`, and the associated `... ≫ h` form cannot be rewritten either. Users must call the lemma by name with explicit `congrArg Over.Hom.left` plumbing, as ComponentFibers.lean does. The private model-level lemma toComponentScheme_comp_componentBaseChangeComparisonModel has the same gap.
findings.proposed_change: Change the attribute to `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]`. The rewrite direction is the existing one: a composite of two canonical maps becomes the single base-changed map. It terminates, since the right side contains no instance of the left pattern. Do the same for the private ...Model lemma.
findings.benefit: `simp` can then normalise composites through the comparison map, including when they occur in the middle of longer chains. This matches how the library treats other canonical-map identities, and it removes manual `rw`/`exact` plumbing downstream.

evidence.declaration: reassoc/simp convention for canonical morphism identities

findings.problem: The simp attribute is inconsistent and unused. This file never calls simp on `.hom` of `specOverIsoOfAlgEquiv`. The lemma is used only through manual `rw`/`rfl` in componentBaseChangeComparisonModelIso_hom and the purelyInseparable variant. ComponentProduct.lean defines a copy of both the private def and the lemma, and there the lemma has no simp attribute and is used by `rw [..., specOverIsoOfAlgEquiv_hom]`. Because the lemma is private and the attribute is inconsistent between the two copies, the simp interface of this helper is unspecified.
findings.proposed_change: Either drop the `@[simp]` here to match the other copy, or keep it and use it. For example, the proofs of the `..._hom` lemmas at lines 561–566 and 1263–1268 could call `simp` or `rw` on it. Better still, move `specOverIsoOfAlgEquiv` and its `_hom` lemma next to `specOverMap` in ComponentScheme.lean as one public declaration with a single deliberate simp status. That also removes the duplicate private copies.
findings.benefit: There is one shared simp lemma with a single, justified status, instead of two private copies that disagree about whether the lemma is simp.
